sowAgain.title: {{crop}}: sow another row
sowAgain.text: The last went in {{weeks}} weeks ago. Sowing again keeps the harvest coming.

todo.nothing: Nothing your garden needs from you this week.
todo.noPlan: Plan your garden and mark what you plant, and this page will list what it needs each week.

thin.title: {{crop}}: thin the seedlings
thin.text: Leave one every {{cm}} cm, so each has room to grow.

support.title: {{crop}}: put up supports
support.text: Canes, netting or twiggy sticks to climb, before they flop. Dwarf kinds can do without.

tieTomato.title: {{crop}}: tie in and pinch out
tieTomato.text: Tie the stem to its cane and pinch out the side shoots, once a week. Bush kinds need neither.

earthUp.title: {{crop}}: earth up
earthUp.text: Draw soil up around the stems, leaving the tops showing. Potatoes in the light turn green.

blanch.title: {{crop}}: earth up the stems
blanch.text: Draw soil up around them a little at a time, for longer white stems.

net.title: {{crop}}: keep under netting
net.text: Fine netting keeps cabbage white butterflies and pigeons off.

pinchBeans.title: {{crop}}: pinch out the tips
pinchBeans.text: Now the first pods are forming. It keeps blackfly away.

pinchSweetPea.title: {{crop}}: pinch out the tips
pinchSweetPea.text: Just above the third pair of leaves, for bushier plants and more flowers.

feed.title: {{crop}}: feed every week or two
feed.text: Now it is flowering and setting fruit, a high-potash feed such as tomato feed keeps the crop coming.

stake.title: {{crop}}: stake the stems
stake.text: Firm the soil around them and tie tall stems to a stake before the autumn winds.

harvestSoon.text: Worked out from the warmth it has had since it went in.

ripen.title: {{crop}}: water less
ripen.text_one: Let the bulbs ripen. They are ready to lift in about a week, once the leaves turn yellow.
ripen.text_other: Let the bulbs ripen. They are ready to lift in about {{count}} weeks, once the leaves turn yellow.

harvest.title: {{crop}}: ready to harvest
harvest.text: It has had the warmth it needs since it went in.

rule.blight: Potatoes and tomatoes share blight; one infects the other.
rule.fennel: Fennel holds back most vegetables; give it a corner of its own.
rule.carrotFly: The onion smell helps hide carrots from carrot fly.
rule.nasturtium: Nasturtiums lure aphids and caterpillars away.
rule.threeSisters: The three sisters: beans climb the corn, squash covers the soil.
rule.basil: A classic pair: basil fills the space under tomatoes.
